items.name: Strive
items.headline: Bitcoin funding plans meet the execution test
items.fact: The Block reported that Strive's CEO discussed potential funding from warrants expiring in October. The larger Bitcoin accumulation scenario was conditional, not his base case.
items.bullCase: Some investors have the right to buy new Strive shares. If they buy, Strive gets more cash. More cash could buy more Bitcoin. That could help, but it does not mean the stock must go up.
items.watchFor: Check company filings for actual warrant exercises and Bitcoin per share. Separate completed purchases from management targets.
items.risk: New shares can dilute existing holders. Bitcoin can fall, and potential warrant proceeds are not guaranteed.

items.name: Hafnia Limited
items.headline: $0.5003 dividend: Oslo and NYSE dates
items.fact: Hafnia declared a Q2 cash dividend of US$0.5003 per share. Oslo trades as HAFNI; NYSE trades as HAFN. Oslo VPS holders receive the NOK equivalent, converted two business days before their payment date. Q2 net profit was $277.8 million, including $39.3 million from vessel sales.
items.bullCase: Hafnia made more money. Its debt is smaller compared with what its ships are worth. That puts the company in a stronger position. It does not guarantee the stock goes up.
items.watchFor: Oslo VPS: ex-dividend September 7, 2026; payment on or about September 23. NYSE / DTC: ex-dividend September 8, 2026; payment on or about September 18. Record date: September 8. The last trading day with dividend rights was September 4 on both markets. Buying on or after the applicable ex-dividend date does not qualify for this payout.
items.risk: This is one quarterly payout, not a guaranteed recurring amount or profit. Share prices can adjust for dividends. Tanker rates are cyclical: booked Q3 rates averaged $30,716 per day for 80% of earning days, below Q2's $44,093. Future earnings and dividends can fall.

sources.label: Hafnia dividend press release · Oslo and NYSE · Aug 28
